header: This is the clarifying question with CHECKBOXES (departments) or RADIO buttons (one doctor, one unit): the types, the rewriting of the person's own question by the ticked option(s), and the test of whether a question is about people. The hospital route uses it (which doctor? which department? which unit?), and so would any future department word that really has to be asked about. I no longer ask about the words "garage" and "refractory": step 55a resolves them (departmentWords.ts). The question that is searched for is the SAME question with the ticked options named, and it must always pass the rules that decide whether to ask, so ticking can never ask again.

members.name: label
doc: I show this next to the checkbox

members.name: phrase
doc: The words the rewritten question uses to name this department

members.name: detail
doc: A second line under the label (a doctor's discipline and unit)

members.name: message
doc: The question I put to the person: it names the word, says what the list holds, and tells what to do

members.name: word
doc: The bare word that is replaced in the question

members.name: question
doc: The question as the person typed it

members.name: none
doc: For "None of these": nothing can be searched, so I show this sentence

members.name: documents
doc: Set only when the person typed just the word; it offers a search of the circulars instead

members.name: legend
doc: What a screen reader hears for the group; the default is "Choose the doctor you mean" for radio buttons and "Tick the department or departments you mean" for checkboxes

members.name: mode
doc: "one" gives RADIO buttons, exactly one option (a doctor); the default "many" gives checkboxes (departments)

members.name: pattern
doc: A regular expression (source) that finds the words to replace, when they are not one plain word ("a mukherjee")

members.name: alternative
doc: Another search the person may want instead (all employees of that name)

symbols.name: isAboutPeopleOrBare
doc: True for a question about people, or for just a word or two ("garage", "garage staff", "central stores department").

symbols.name: queryFor
symbols.sig: export function queryFor(ask: DepartmentAsk, ticked: string[]): string
doc: Builds the question to search for when these options are ticked; returns "" when none is.

behaviours: one option ticked: the question names its six rows by name and code, the rest of the question is untouched
a question about people has no documents option; a bare word has one
three options, each a REAL row of the list: the same name and code as in the 300 rows
...and they are all the refractory rows of the list (no other row has the word)
one ticked: the question names it by name and code
all three ticked: a comma and an 'and', in the order of the list whatever the order of the ticks
three options have 7 combinations of ticks, and every one is possible (radio buttons could offer 3)
no loop: ticks [${s}] -> "${q.slice(0, 60)}..." is left alone by the department words
no loop for the garage question either
a pattern finds the words to replace
if the words are not found, the phrase is added at the end
